column3: One of China's oldest museums, it holds Shang bronzes, jade, and the Jiahu bone flutes, among the oldest playable instruments in the world.
The remains of a city wall from the Shang dynasty about 3,500 years ago, beside modern Zhengzhou.
A park on the south bank of the Yellow River, with large statues of the legendary emperors Yan and Huang on a mountain slope.
A twin-towered memorial in the middle of Zhengzhou, honoring a railway workers' strike in 1923.
The famous Chan Buddhist temple at the foot of Mount Song, where kung fu is said to have begun. Monks still train in its courtyards.
One of the Five Sacred Mountains of China, with Shaolin Temple, Zhongyue Temple and old observatory on its slopes.
A temple for the god of Mount Song, the central sacred mountain, with halls of the Daoist tradition, and giant old cypress trees.
Wide hand-pulled noodles in a rich mutton broth, with seaweed and tofu, the staple of Zhengzhou. Cooks pull and stretch the dough just before it goes in the pot.
A thick, peppery soup of beef or lamb, with wheat gluten and spices, eaten at breakfast with fried dough.
Large steamed buns filled with a pocket of hot broth, so you must bite carefully and sip the soup first.
Noodles tossed in flour and steamed with vegetables, then dressed with garlic sauce, a simple home favorite.
The martial arts of Shaolin monks, trained for centuries, include fast fists, staff fighting and strong stances.
Henan opera, with strong, high singing, is the most widely performed opera in China, with fans across the country.
Thousands of Buddhist carvings line a limestone cliff by the Yi River, including a giant seated Buddha about 17 meters tall. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
The first Buddhist temple in China, said to have been founded in the first century CE, when white horses carried Buddhist scriptures to Luoyang.
A temple and tomb for the general Guan Yu, whose head is said to be buried here, honored as a god of loyalty.
A museum that tells the long story of Luoyang, a capital for many dynasties, with Tang tomb figures and Luoyang's treasures.
A huge reconstructed gate of the Sui and Tang palace in Luoyang, a sign of the capital's grandeur.
A traditional banquet of about 24 dishes, many of them soups, which are served one after another, each new dish replacing the last.
A soup of eggs and pork, poached gently so that it does not need to be flipped, served in a bowl, and a Luoyang water-banquet dish.
A sweet pastry made with peony petals, a delicate Luoyang treat that reflects the city's love for its flower.
Every spring, Luoyang holds a flower festival when thousands of peonies are in bloom, and crowds fill the city's parks.
Tang sancai are lead-glazed pottery figures of horses, camels and ladies in green, yellow and white glaze, once placed in tombs.
A palace hall on a high platform beside a lake in Kaifeng, built where the palace of the Song dynasty stood.
A tall brown pagoda covered in glazed bricks, built in the Song dynasty. It looks like iron but is made of ceramic.
A major Buddhist temple of the Song era in Kaifeng, once the largest in the capital and home to a busy market.
Delicate soup dumplings with thin skin from a famous Kaifeng shop, filled with a rich broth.
Carp from the Yellow River braised in a rich, savory sauce, a classic Kaifeng dish.
A sweet, crumbly snack made from peanuts and sugar, sold at the busy night market.
Kaifeng's city flower is the chrysanthemum, and every autumn the city holds a show with thousands of blooms.
The ruins of the last capital of the Shang dynasty, where oracle bone inscriptions were found. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and the home of China's earliest writing.
A museum on the history of Chinese writing, from oracle bones to modern characters, in Anyang.
A canal that villagers cut into the cliffs of the Taihang Mountains in the 1960s to bring water to dry land, a symbol of determination.
A hearty stew with flat sweet potato noodles, vegetables, and meat, a typical winter dish in Anyang.
A braised chicken from Daokou, so tender that the bones can be pulled out whole. It has been famous for hundreds of years.
Oracle bone script, the earliest known form of Chinese writing, was carved on turtle shells and bones for divination about 3,000 years ago.
A canyon park with waterfalls, cliff paths and clear pools, often called a green gem in northern Henan.
The Huai yam is a famous Henan product that is used in soups and in traditional medicine, valued for its smooth texture.
Tai chi is a slow, flowing martial art, born in Chenjiagou village in Henan, and now practiced worldwide for health.
Cattle from Nanyang, with tender beef that is braised or grilled, is a local specialty.
Jade carved in Zhenping and Nanyang is a craft that has been practiced for centuries, from small pendants to large sculptures.
A crisp, layered sesame flatbread, often filled with meat, baked fresh in Shangqiu.
A large lake with green islands and hills near Xinyang, a favorite place for a break.
One of China's famous green teas, with slender, curled leaves and a fresh, mellow taste, grown in the hills of Xinyang.
Sweet, soft chestnuts from the Dabie Mountains, roasted in autumn.
A local peanut variety with rich, sweet taste, grown in the hills of Lushan.
